distribution.reason: Local virtual-card candidate. Observed closure flags (virt-card patch without an explicit grant, LGPL glib, GPL-2.0-or-later dual-license options in TF-PSA-Crypto/framework sources), actual-layer/generated-content review and digest-bound source-companion delivery remain incomplete; checker/consumer/proxy admission is separate.

constraints: Linux amd64/glibc, virtual PIV card only. YubiKey hardware, other readers, other backends, FIPS claims and other architectures/libcs are excluded. This qualifies libykcs11 against CanoKey, never YubiKey hardware.

Both channels source-build unpatched yubico-piv-tool (release 2.7.3, rolling 2.7.3-5-gc987afb) with system OpenSSL 3.5.7 libcrypto.so.3; no legacy provider and no from-source OpenSSL. The CanoKey-core backend pin (e4a756d6 plus 7 pinned submodules) is shared across channels with two virt-card patches (target without sanitizers; IFD entry-trace silenced, warnings kept); upstream PKCS#11 semantics are unchanged.

Basic runtime has the module, libykpiv, yubico-piv-tool, the virt-card IFD handler with its reader.conf entry, pcscd, the openssl CLI, base libraries and the exact extracted closure (7 whole packages, audited with ldd receipts). USB CCID drivers, the polkitd/dbus daemons, opensc, Python, checker, datasets and tracing are excluded; nothing links them.
The caller UID may be root or non-root with any primary group; both are qualified. No NSS wrapper or fixed group is required.

Bind writable /var/lib/p11lab; private ephemeral /run/p11lab and writable /tmp (fixed virtual-card flash path) are required. /run/pcscd is an in-image symlink into the control tmpfs so the fixed daemon socket path works without a caller mount. Never share /run or /tmp with another runtime. Each shard/client owns a separate volume, container and daemon. Logs and pid state live under /run; the slot-9a key, certificate, lease and marker persist under /var/lib/p11lab/ykcs11.

The card is factory-fresh every operation by construction (reset on daemon load, not a failure mode). First init generates the slot-9a P-256 key and self-signed certificate into caller state; every operation re-personalizes the fresh card with the caller PIN/PUK and re-imports the stored identity, so card objects are byte-stable across operations. Persistent-token requests are unsupported.

Caller user/SO PINs are the PIV PIN/PUK, each 6..8 bytes single-line; init, health and exec all require both because every operation re-personalizes a fresh card. No baked caller credentials or initialized card state. The management key stays the public factory default and is never passed on argv or stdin.

The token label is fixed natively as YubiKey PIV #0 at slot 0, token-present index 0; P11LAB_LABEL defaults to it and any other value is refused. SO (PUK) login is not a PKCS#11 credential: C_Login as SO takes the user PIN or a management-key hex, and the PUK serves only PIN unblock and rotation.

init/health/exec supervise pcscd for that operation only: subreaper adoption, volume/control leases, socket plus exactly-one-CanoKey-reader plus Yubico-handshake plus native pre-login token readiness, daemon-death detection, signal forwarding, bounded logs and bounded terminate/kill/reap. exec retains pcscd for the complete application lifetime and preserves argv/status.

Provisioning uses only pinned yubico-piv-tool and openssl argv with caller secrets on bounded private stdin pipes, never argv/logs. The provision log carries only prompt names and native status lines. A card that cannot answer the Yubico handshake is refused before any PKCS#11 call.

Unknown/hidden entries, unsafe links/hardlinks/modes, changed non-secret configuration, stale daemon debris, missing key/certificate and busy state are refused before native open. Failures retain partial state for investigation.

The general-token profile is retained after native P-256 independent verification and altered-message rejection in both channels; other slots, wider mechanisms, multi-client concurrency, other readers/backends and provider-wide qualification are not asserted.

All runtime/consumer/checker/proxy artifacts remain blocked for distribution. Preserve exact provider sources, the 8-repository CanoKey closure, Debian closure sources/notices and generated build inputs; source admission, public delivery and publication are separate gates.
